title: The pluperfect
topic: pluscuamperfecto; what had happened earlier in the past
why: After the imperfect and the indefinido (units 7 and 8), the pluperfect completes the storytelling toolkit: había + participle to say what had happened before another moment in the past. The lesson wraps up the unit “Imagining and regretting” and prepares reported speech in unit 18, where it's used to report what people said.

Había + participle: I had done

Good news: the Spanish pluperfect (pluscuamperfecto) works almost exactly like the English past perfect, “I had done.” Take haber in the imperfect and add the past participle.

haberexample: empezar
yohabíahabía empezado
túhabíashabías empezado
él, ella, ustedhabíahabía empezado
nosotros, nosotrashabíamoshabíamos empezado
vosotros, vosotrashabíaishabíais empezado
ellos, ellas, ustedeshabíanhabían empezado

As with the pretérito perfecto and the past conditional, the auxiliary is always haber, just as English always uses “had”: “he had left” = había salido, “we had gotten up” = nos habíamos levantado. The participle never agrees: Ellas habían llegado.

Where do ya, todavía no, nunca and pronouns go?

Nothing goes between había and the participle (unlike English “I had already left”). Ya, todavía no and nunca usually go before; pronouns go before había.

Cuando llegué, Lucía ya se había ido.When I arrived, Lucía had already left.
Nunca lo había visto tan contento.I had never seen him so happy.

Three forms not to confuse

SpanishEnglishTense
he comidoI have eatenpretérito perfecto
había comidoI had eatenpluperfect
habría comidoI would have eatenpast conditional

You already know había with another meaning: “there was / there were” (Había mucha gente). Followed by a participle, it's the pluperfect: Había llovido (it had rained).

", "

The past of the past

The pluperfect shows that an action happened before another moment in the past. Compare:

SentenceWhat happened
Cuando llegué, la película empezó.I arrive, then the movie starts.
Cuando llegué, la película ya había empezado.The movie starts, then I arrive: I missed the beginning.

Nunca he… / Nunca había…

English makes the same distinction between “I've never seen” and “I had never seen”:

Nunca he visto la nieve.I've never seen snow. (up to today)
Hasta aquel viaje, nunca había visto la nieve.Before that trip, I had never seen snow. (up to that moment in the past)

Phrases that call for it

  • ya / todavía no in a story: Cuando llamé, todavía no habían cenado. (When I called, they hadn't had dinner yet.)
  • darse cuenta de que: Me di cuenta de que había olvidado el pasaporte. (I realized I had forgotten my passport.)
  • porque, for an earlier cause: Estaba cansada porque había trabajado diez horas. (She was tired because she had worked ten hours.)
  • hasta entonces, hasta aquel día: Hasta entonces, nunca había hablado en público. (Until then, I had never spoken in public.)

In speech, with antes or después, the order of events is already clear and Spaniards often just use the indefinido, as English often uses the simple past: Comimos después de visitar el museo. The pluperfect becomes essential when nothing else shows what happened first.

", "

Telling a story with three past tenses

To tell a story, you now have three past tenses, each with its own role, much like English “was doing / used to do,” the simple past and the past perfect:

TenseRoleExample
imperfectothe background, states, habitsEra viernes y hacía calor.
indefinidothe events that move the story forwardLlegamos al restaurante a las diez.
pluscuamperfectowhat had happened beforeHabíamos reservado una mesa.

A ruined evening in Granada

Era viernes y hacía muchísimo calor en Granada.It was Friday and it was incredibly hot in Granada.
Habíamos reservado una mesa en un restaurante con vistas a la Alhambra.We had booked a table at a restaurant with a view of the Alhambra.
Pero cuando llegamos, vimos que estaba cerrado: el dueño se había ido de vacaciones.But when we got there, we saw it was closed: the owner had gone on vacation.
Entonces buscamos otro sitio, y en ese momento me di cuenta de que había dejado la cartera en el hotel.So we looked for another place, and at that moment I realized I had left my wallet at the hotel.
Al final cenamos un bocadillo en un banco. ¡Nunca me había reído tanto!In the end, we had a sandwich on a bench for dinner. I had never laughed so much!

Before each verb, ask yourself: is it the background (imperfect), an event (indefinido) or something that had happened earlier (pluperfect)?
